name: two-phase-artifact-wiring-must-be-verified-end-to-end
description: Many features require a two-phase registration: first declare/create an artifact (a migration file, a SQL table, a constant), then wire it into the consuming code (register in the array, reference in application logic, include in a collection). Either phase succeeding without the other is a silent partial failure. Session evidence shows this pattern recurring across migration file registration, migration-table-to-app-code linkage, and const-to-array wiring.
use_when: A feature requires both creating an artifact (file, table, constant) AND registering/referencing it in a separate location
Adding a new SQL migration file that must also appear in the MIGRATIONS array or equivalent runner config
Any pattern where a list or registry must stay in sync with a set of on-disk files
invariants: Every declared artifact must have exactly one corresponding wiring entry; orphans in either direction are failures
produces: Blocking CI check that lists all orphaned artifacts
Explicit error at startup or test time when wiring is incomplete

name: probe-external-system-parameters-at-runtime-not-hardcode
description: Parameters that are owned by an external system — vector dimensions, model output sizes, API version capabilities — must be discovered by a live probe call at startup or collection-creation time, not hardcoded as constants. The live system is the authoritative source of truth; a hardcoded value diverges silently whenever system configuration changes (model swap, server upgrade, env switch), producing type mismatches or subtle data corruption that are not caught until query time.
use_when: Creating a vector collection whose dimension must match the embedding model's actual output size
Configuring any pipeline stage whose size, shape, or capability is determined by an external service rather than the local codebase
The external system's parameters can change via a configuration or model swap without a code change
invariants: The value used for local configuration must always equal the value returned by a live probe of the same external system in the same environment
produces: Fail-fast startup error if the probe cannot reach the external system
Runtime-discovered configuration value that stays correct across system upgrades

name: When resuming a session, pick up the last (preference)
description: Standing user preference: When resuming a session, pick up the last task immediately without acknowledging the summary, recapping what was happening, or using transitional phrases like ''I''ll continue''.

name: All retrieval and quality measurement must drive the (preference)
description: Standing user preference: All retrieval and quality measurement must drive the real running MCP server over HTTP end-to-end; in-process reconstruction is never acceptable as a substitute.

name: rust-cargo-bin-target-missing-docker-build-failure
description: When a Rust crate declares [lib] and src/main.rs but no explicit [[bin]], cargo auto-names the binary after the package name; a Dockerfile using --bin with a different name fails with 'no bin target named X'.
use_when: cargo build --bin {X} fails with 'no bin target named {X} in default-run packages
Dockerfile uses '--bin ${BIN}' as a build-arg and a service exits 101
Rust workspace has a crate that declares [lib] and src/main.rs but no [[bin]]
Multi-service Rust workspace with one shared Dockerfile parameterized by BIN
invariants: A crate that declares both [lib] and a binary MUST have an explicit [[bin]] section or cargo uses the package name as the binary name
The [[bin]] name field must exactly match the value passed to cargo --bin and to Docker's BIN build-arg
produces: A binary artifact named exactly {expected-bin-name} under target/{profile}/
A successful Docker service image built via the BIN-parameterized Dockerfile

name: orphaned-migration-file-detection
description: SQL migration files that exist on disk but are never registered in the migration runner's const/array silently skip schema changes; audit the runner array against the migrations directory before adding new migrations.
use_when: Adding a new migration and suspecting prior ones may be unregistered
Schema columns expected from a migration are missing in the live DB despite the SQL file existing
Migration ordering test fails after adding a new entry
invariants: The set of .sql files on disk must equal the set of entries in the migration runner array.
Orphan registrations must be idempotent — IF NOT EXISTS on all DDL.
produces: A migration runner where every .sql file is registered; no silent schema gaps

name: serialize-shared-file-todos-across-agent-batches
description: When orchestrating parallel agents, any two todos that touch the same file must be placed in different serial batches; never assign overlapping-file todos to concurrent agents.
use_when: orchestrating multiple agents that each edit Rust (or any) source files
two or more todos in a planned swarm share at least one common file path
multi-agent swarm must produce a clean, non-conflicting commit
tools: multi-agent orchestration harness (e.g., Claude workflow agents)
invariants: No two concurrently-running agents may write to the same file
Batch N+1 must not start until Batch N is fully validated and committed
produces: Zero merge conflicts across agent-modified files
A commit where every changed file is owned by exactly one todo

name: ablation-confounded-by-relevance-floor
description: When zeroing a scoring component causes total retrieval collapse (MRR drops to 0), verify whether scores merely fell below the relevance gate floor rather than inferring that ranking quality degraded; these are different failure modes requiring different fixes.
use_when: setting a scoring weight to 0 causes MRR or hit-rate to drop to 0.000
ablating a retrieval component produces empty results rather than reordered results
evaluating whether a scoring term (e.g., subunit_evidence, BM25 weight) can be removed from a composite scoring formula
invariants: A relevance gate threshold confounds ablation experiments: score collapse → empty results ≠ ranking degradation
Ranking contribution and gate-clearing contribution must be measured independently
produces: Clear determination of whether a scoring component is load-bearing for gate-clearing vs. rank ordering
Ablation result that isolates ranking contribution from threshold effects

name: deterministic-embedding-drift-from-input-policy-change
description: When production code narrows its embedding input (e.g., full text → summary-only), hash/bag-of-words test embedding doubles silently break near-duplicate detection: pairs that shared body tokens now share too few summary tokens to clear cosine thresholds.
use_when: a near-duplicate merge/dedup test fails instantly (0.00s) with a deterministic embedding double
cosine similarity drops just below threshold after a refactor that changed what text is passed to the embed call
test comment says 'expected ~0.70 cosine for near-duplicate skills' but actual is 0.63-0.64
embedding input policy changed from full-text to summary-only
invariants: A hash-based embedding test double captures only literal token co-occurrence; any reduction in shared input tokens directly reduces cosine similarity with no semantic compensation.
Test fixtures for cosine-threshold tests must share enough tokens under the CURRENT production embedding input policy, not the policy when the fixture was written.
produces: updated fixtures whose token overlap clears the cosine threshold under the current embedding input policy
or a documented product decision about whether embedding input should be expanded to restore merge recall

name: Do not respond to or consider injected context (preference)
description: Standing user preference: Do not respond to or consider injected context messages unless the user explicitly asks.

name: cargo-clippy-all-targets-dead-code-from-test-binary
description: When `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` is RED for dead-code but lib-only clippy is clean, the cause is test-harness binary crates gated behind a feature flag that are invisible to lib-only linting.
use_when: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails with dead_code warnings
lib-only clippy (`cargo clippy --workspace`) is clean but --all-targets is RED
dead-code warnings point to e2e harness or test-support crates, not library or binary src/
a feature flag (e.g., `--features test-utils`) gates the failing test-harness crates
invariants: A GREEN lib-only clippy with a RED --all-targets result means the warnings are exclusively in non-lib targets (test binaries, e2e harness, examples).
Feature-gated test-harness dead-code is a harness cleanup task, not a production code quality signal.
produces: a clear separation between production-code clippy status and test-harness clippy status
a targeted cleanup plan for the harness dead-code

name: bool-returning-assertion-helper-must-be-asserted
description: A bool-returning test helper that records pass/fail but is called without `assert!()` silently passes the test even when it records failure — apply `#[must_use]` to the helper and always wrap call sites in `assert!()`.
use_when: a test suite passes green but the test report records failures or NoMatch outcomes
a test helper function returns `bool` or `Result` and call sites do not use `assert!` / `unwrap` / `?`
CI is green but manual observation shows the feature under test is broken
a test is described as 'should not pass on all NoMatch' — check whether the assertion helper is actually enforced
artifacts: any test file with bool-returning assert helpers
invariants: Every call to a bool-returning assertion helper MUST be wrapped in `assert!()` or equivalent — a bare function call silently discards the result in Rust.
A test that records `Failed` in a report but exits `ok` is a broken test, not a passing one.
produces: test suite that actually panics (fails) when assertion helpers record failures
previously-hidden failures surfaced as explicit test failures on the next run

name: path-starts-with-requires-symmetric-canonicalization
description: Path::starts_with silently fails under symlinked working directories (e.g. Docker bind mounts) when one side is canonicalized and the other is not; canonicalize both sides at load time, not at comparison time.
use_when: path.starts_with(scope_path) returns false unexpectedly
Docker bind mounts or dev-container symlinked working directories cause scope matching to fail
global scope paths work but project scope paths silently return no_match
one path was canonicalized at ingestion time and another was taken from current_dir() without canonicalization
artifacts: *.rs files performing path prefix scope checks
invariants: Both operands of starts_with must share the same canonical form for the check to be reliable.
Canonicalization must happen at load/ingestion time, not on the comparison hot path.
produces: Correct scope matching under symlinked or bind-mounted working directories

name: tokio-spawn-no-joinhandle-teardown-db-race
description: When async writers are spawned via tokio::spawn without storing the JoinHandle, a teardown/TRUNCATE step will race their RowExclusive DB locks and hang; fix by draining/awaiting the writers before teardown.
use_when: test teardown hangs under default config but passes when a logging/writing flag is disabled
TRUNCATE ... CASCADE hangs in test cleanup and async writers are present
tokio::spawn is used for DB writes without a stored JoinHandle
test suite passes only with MCP_USAGE_LOGGING=off or equivalent env bypass
invariants: All tokio::spawn tasks that hold RowExclusive (or any write) DB locks must be fully drained before any DDL or TRUNCATE is issued in teardown.
Storing no JoinHandle is a silent correctness bug when teardown order matters — it must not be papered over with an env-var flag.
produces: A test suite that is green under default configuration without any env-var bypass

name: near-zero-cosine-score-suspects
description: When embedding-based retrieval returns correct top hits but with near-zero cosine similarity scores (~0.01–0.03), the two root causes to check are: (1) vectors not L2-normalized before dot product, (2) query encoded without the required task prefix while documents were encoded with it (or vice versa).
use_when: embedding retrieval scores near zero (~0.01–0.03) for correct top hits
cosine similarity compressed near zero even when query semantically matches skill text
nomic-embed-text or other task-prefix embedding model shows low scores
eq.3 scores are tiny even for correct retrievals
invariants: Query and document embeddings must use matching task prefixes for asymmetric models.
Vectors must be L2-normalized before a dot product is used as a cosine similarity proxy.
produces: identified root cause (normalization vs prefix mismatch) and, after fix, cosine scores in the expected 0.6–0.99 range for strong semantic matches

name: isolate-timing-test-to-diagnose-load-flake
description: When a latency or timing test fails during a run with concurrent background activity, run it in isolation to distinguish a load-induced flake from a real regression before acting.
use_when: A latency or timing test fails during a run with concurrent background activity (downloads, parallel builds)
The test failure disappears when run in isolation
The test touches a code path unchanged by the current diff
invariants: A test that passes in isolation but fails under load is load-sensitive, not a code regression.
Do not declare a flake without first confirming: (a) passes in isolation, AND (b) the code path under test is unchanged.
produces: Clear determination: load-induced flake vs. real regression
Actionable todo for hardening the timing assertion

name: gate-parallel-agents-on-file-overlap
description: Before scheduling two agent tasks in parallel, check whether they edit any of the same files; if they share even one file, they must run sequentially to avoid conflicting commits.
use_when: scheduling two or more agent tasks to run in parallel in a multi-agent workflow
a parallel batch produces merge conflicts in files that multiple agents modified
planning ticket batches for a feature branch where multiple tasks touch the same module
invariants: Two agents that write to the same file must never run concurrently in the same worktree.
Sequential dependency edges must be recorded in the batch plan before agents are dispatched.
produces: A batch schedule where every parallel group has zero file overlap, eliminating intra-batch commit conflicts

name: read-before-write-file-edit
description: Resolve a 'file not read yet' write error by reading the target file first, then applying edits to the correct offsets.

name: inspect-current-state-before-mutating
description: Before performing any mutation, recovery, or transformation, first read/audit the current state of the target artefact. Acting on assumed or stale state leads to tool errors (file-not-read guard), data loss, or incorrect recovery paths. The inspection step is never optional even when the state 'seems obvious'.
use_when: About to edit a source file via any tool
Recovering from a partial or failed run where intermediate outputs may exist
Transforming or migrating existing data whose current shape is uncertain
Resuming work after a context gap or agent restart
invariants: No mutation is issued against an artefact that has not been explicitly observed in the current session.
produces: Reduced tool errors due to stale-state assumptions
Correct salvage decisions in partial-failure recovery

name: contamination-vs-precision-triangulation-for-no-match-failures
description: When a 'should-not-match / NoMatch' assertion fails but a dedicated precision/negatives test passes in the same test run, the failure is shared-corpus contamination (corpus state), NOT a systemic precision regression in the retrieval/matching code.
use_when: a test asserting at least one NoMatch response receives zero NoMatch instead
should-miss prompt unexpectedly matches something in the corpus
retrieval or skill-matching test fails in a sequential run but seems fine in isolation
invariants: If negatives-test passes and should-miss fails in the same run, the discriminating variable is corpus state, not matching logic
produces: A classification: ''corpus contamination (isolation bug)'' vs. ''precision regression in matching code'', with a reproducible isolation test

name: silent-ok-does-not-mean-contract-satisfied
description: Infrastructure APIs and tooling regularly return success (200 OK, zero exit code, no exception) without validating the semantic contract of the call. Qdrant's ensure_collection silently ignores a dimension mismatch on an existing collection; docker-compose emits an empty string instead of erroring on a missing env var; SQL migration runners skip unregistered files without complaint. Trusting success codes as proof-of-correctness produces subtle, late-breaking runtime failures that are difficult to attribute.
use_when: Calling idempotent infrastructure APIs (ensure_*, create_or_update, upsert) where the system may silently ignore parameter mismatches on existing resources
Reading configuration from environment variables whose absence results in an empty-string Ok rather than an Err
Running schema migration tooling whose success code does not guarantee all registered artifacts were applied
invariants: A success code is necessary but never sufficient proof that the semantic contract was satisfied — a structural probe is always required
produces: Fail-fast startup errors on contract violations
Post-operation structural assertions that catch silent mismatches

name: multi-layer-atomic-propagation
description: Whenever a system enforces invariants across multiple coupled layers (e.g., SQL schema + layered migration tests; CQRS command handler + related-entity persistence coordinator), every addition or change must be propagated atomically to ALL layers in the same unit of work. Partial propagation leaves the system in a broken, inconsistent state that either fails loudly at CI or silently corrupts data.
use_when: Adding a new SQL migration to a codebase with layered migration tests
Adding persistence for a new related entity (edges, tags, associations) to an existing CQRS write path
Extending any system where schema, handler logic, and tests share an invariant that must hold simultaneously
invariants: No layer that participates in a cross-layer invariant is left in its old state when the other layers have been updated.
produces: Green CI on first pass
No partial-state windows where schema and tests disagree
Clean CQRS write paths with explicit coordinator boundaries

name: migration-test-triple-update
description: When adding a new SQL migration to a suite that has layered migration tests, update all three test layers atomically: the ordering test, the live migration assertion list, and the TRUNCATE/cleanup guard test.
use_when: adding a new SQL migration file to a multi-test migration suite
test suite has separate ordering, live, and TRUNCATE/cleanup migration tests
migration creates a new table that must be covered by TRUNCATE cleanup
invariants: All three test layers must be updated in the same change; a partial update will cause one layer to go stale silently
produces: All three migration test groups pass after the new migration is added

name: sparse-vector-test-must-assert-weight-values-not-just-index-count
description: Tests for sparse-vector (BM25/TF-IDF) encoding must assert on term weight values for repeated-term inputs, not only on index/key uniqueness, because accumulation bugs pass index-count checks silently.
use_when: writing or reviewing tests for a BM25 / TF-IDF / sparse vector encoder
a function builds a HashMap of term → weight and the test is named '*deduplicates*
code uses `HashMap::entry().or_insert(0.0) += 1.0` for sparse term weights
invariants: A test named 'deduplicates_repeated_terms' must assert that the weight for a repeated term equals the weight for a single occurrence, not a multiple of it.
Index-count-only assertions cannot detect weight-accumulation bugs.
produces: A test suite that catches `or_insert += accumulation` bugs for repeated terms in sparse-vector encoding.

name: compare-retrieval-arms-top10
description: Boot two retrieval backend arms (dense vs hybrid) in Docker, capture top-10 results for held-out queries against the live MCP server, diff the captures, and record the owner's architectural decision in project memory.

name: Always read transcripts from a temporary PostgreSQL table (preference)

name: An MRR/nDCG score of 80 is an aspiration (preference)
description: Standing user preference: An MRR/nDCG score of 80 is an aspiration target and must never be faked or artificially marked as passing.

name: orchestration-side-revalidation-after-parallel-agents
description: After parallel agents execute in a shared working tree, always revalidate the combined state with compile+test+lint before trusting any individual agent's pass/fail self-report — even when agents touch disjoint files.
use_when: parallel agents execute fixes in a shared working tree (not isolated worktrees)
one agent reports a clippy/build error referencing a symbol introduced by another in-flight agent
agents are file-disjoint but crate-level lint runs across all files in the crate
invariants: Orchestration-side combined-tree validation must run AFTER all parallel agents complete and BEFORE any agent's reported outcome is marked authoritative.
A crate-wide lint/build check in a shared tree will see all in-flight symbol changes from concurrent agents, regardless of which files each agent touched.
produces: A single authoritative compile+test+lint verdict for the combined changes of all parallel agents
Correctly diagnosed false-positive errors that were cross-agent contamination rather than real defects

name: container-hook-absolute-path-resolution-options
description: When a hook system (e.g. Claude Code SessionEnd) passes absolute host filesystem paths to a containerized service, the path won't resolve inside the container unless the mount path matches; three viable escape hatches exist with different trade-off profiles.
use_when: hook system passes `{{transcript_path}}` or similar absolute host path variable to an MCP/containerized service
validator rejects absolute paths but the hook has no relative-path variable available
container mounts a host directory at a different path than its host-side location
invariants: A content-bypass queue (option c) MUST be paired with an FS-scan reconcile pass; otherwise transcripts produced before a crash are silently lost.
The trust boundary (no path traversal outside the designated root) must be preserved regardless of which option is chosen.
produces: A path-resolution strategy that allows the containerized service to read hook-delivered file refs without path-validation rejections

name: pre-commit-gitignore-silent-exclusion-check
description: After staging files, verify the staged count matches expectation and explicitly confirm any missing files are intentionally gitignored — never silently lose deliverables.
use_when: staged file count is lower than expected after `git add -A`
committing output from a multi-agent session where many files were created
`git status` shows fewer files than you authored
invariants: Every file expected to be a deliverable must be either staged or explicitly confirmed as intentionally ignored before the commit proceeds.
produces: A commit that contains exactly the intended deliverables, with all omissions explained

name: zero-second-test-failure-is-deterministic-not-flaky
description: A test that fails in 0.00s before any external service call is a deterministic precondition/data issue, not LLM or network flakiness; stash current changes and rerun to isolate whether it is a pre-existing regression.
use_when: a test in a supposedly self-contained suite fails with 'finished in 0.00s
a failure appears in a test that uses test doubles (DeterministicEmbeddingService, AlwaysEquivalentVerifier) and no real services
need to determine if a CI failure was introduced by the current branch or was pre-existing
invariants: A 0.00s failure cannot have reached any async I/O or LLM call; the root cause is local and deterministic.
produces: a confirmed verdict: pre-existing vs. regression introduced by current branch

name: ollama-embedding-2048-token-batch-limit
description: Ollama caps embedding batch input at ~2048 tokens even when the underlying model (e.g. nomic-embed-text) advertises 8192; exceeding this returns HTTP 500. Add a char-budget truncation guard with loud warn! at the embedding service layer.
use_when: Ollama embedding call returns HTTP 500 or 422 on long inputs
embedding input is built by concatenating name + description + full document body
nomic-embed-text or similar model is served via Ollama and input grows with document size
invariants: Ollama embedding batch limit is ~2048 tokens regardless of the model's advertised context length
Truncation must be loud (warn!) — never silent
produces: Embedding calls succeed on long inputs; truncation events appear in logs; no silent data loss

name: reread-file-before-edit-on-conflict
description: When an edit fails with 'file modified since read', re-read the file at its current state before retrying the write to avoid stale-content conflicts.

name: No stubs, fakes, placeholders, hardcoded canned data, or (preference)
description: Standing user preference: No stubs, fakes, placeholders, hardcoded canned data, or silent fallbacks in production or non-unit-test paths — fail loud instead. Mocks are only permitted behind `#[cfg(test)]` (or language-equivalent test-only gating). When existing violations are found, surface them with file:line cleanup todos rather than silently working around them.

name: file-overlap-clustering-before-execution-batching
description: Before dispatching a batch of todo/fix agents, enumerate the exact files each task touches, group tasks into overlap clusters, serialize execution within each cluster, and only parallelize across clusters.
use_when: dispatching multiple fix agents in a single pass against a shared working tree
triaging a list of todos before deciding which to execute in one batch
a large planned refactor and several smaller cleanups all touch the same file
invariants: No two agents in the same parallel batch may modify the same file.
Before folding a small task into a larger deferred refactor, confirm the larger refactor is actually planned and tracked — do not silently drop the small task.
produces: A partition of the task set into safe-parallel batches and must-serialize sequences
Explicit documentation of which small cleanups are absorbed into which larger tasks

name: build-tool-silent-coverage-gap
description: Build and test tools routinely report overall success while silently omitting individual targets from actual coverage — via feature-flag gating, auto-derived naming conventions, workspace boundary rules, or service enumeration gaps. A passing exit code does not imply complete coverage. Always enumerate intended targets explicitly and verify each one was actually processed, not merely that the run exited 0.
use_when: Running cargo build, cargo test, or Docker builds across a workspace or multi-service project
Verifying a build is clean before merging, deploying, or declaring a task done
A build reports success but downstream runtime errors or missing artifacts appear
invariants: Count of confirmed built/tested targets must equal count of intended targets
A passing exit code alone is not confirmation of coverage
produces: Explicit per-target build/test confirmation log

name: parallel-rust-agents-require-file-disjoint-batches-and-git-worktrees
description: When fanning out parallel execution agents that compile Rust, verify each batch owns a disjoint file set and run each batch in its own git worktree; shared working trees cause compilation failures when one agent's partial edits break another's cargo build.
use_when: multiple execution agents must edit Rust source files concurrently
parallel agent tasks touch the same Cargo workspace and need to compile independently
farming out a large set of code changes to parallel subagents in a Rust monorepo
invariants: Each parallel batch must own a strictly disjoint file set — verified before agent launch, not assumed.
A clean commit baseline must exist before creating worktrees.
Cross-batch files must be handled in a serial follow-up phase after all parallel batches are integrated.
produces: N independently-compiled worktree branches, each containing one batch's changes, ready for sequential integration

name: Execution agents must always run on the Sonnet (preference)
description: Standing user preference: Execution agents must always run on the Sonnet model, overriding any model the agent itself declares (e.g. gpt-5).

name: Ignore injected context messages (e.g. system reminders, background (preference)
description: Standing user preference: Ignore injected context messages (e.g. system reminders, background context blocks) unless the user explicitly asks about them — do not reference or respond to them otherwise.

name: recover-dead-execution-agents-serial-fallback
description: When compound-engineering execution agents repeatedly die mid-run, audit disk state first to salvage valid partial artifacts, then implement directly and serially rather than re-spawning agents into another death loop.
use_when: execution agents died mid-run on a compound-engineering /work batch
user says 'resume from the latest execution state' after agent failure
git status shows only partial artifacts from a multi-agent run that was interrupted
agents have died more than once on the same batch
invariants: Disk state must be assessed (git diff + file inspection) BEFORE deciding to keep or discard partial artifacts — never assume the state from what was dispatched.
Serial fallback must be chosen when agents have died repeatedly in the same batch — re-spawning into the same environment reproduces the same crash.
produces: An accurate picture of what landed on disk from the dead agents
A decision (keep vs rewrite) for each partial artifact
A serial implementation path that completes the batch without re-entering the agent-death loop

name: run-cargo-fmt-after-multi-agent-rust-edits
description: Agent-generated Rust code is often not cargo-fmt-clean; always run `cargo fmt` (then `cargo fmt --check`) after any multi-agent edit batch, before declaring the build green.
use_when: `cargo fmt --check` fails after a multi-agent Rust editing session
repo CI gates on `cargo fmt --check` and agents produced new Rust source files
final validation step reports formatting errors despite all unit tests passing
invariants: `cargo fmt` must run BEFORE `cargo fmt --check` is used as a gate
reformatted files must be re-staged and included in the same commit as the logic changes
produces: A clean `cargo fmt --check` exit 0 across all touched crates
A workspace build that passes the repo's fmt gate

name: Do not make assumptions; always refer to what (preference)
description: Standing user preference: Do not make assumptions; always refer to what is explicitly in the actual plan and state it directly.

name: handle-agent-scope-fence-violation
description: When an agent exceeds its scope fence but produces mechanically correct out-of-scope changes, validate each out-of-fence file independently, document the violation in the work log, and flag it honestly to the user rather than blindly reverting correct work.
use_when: an agent fixed files outside its explicitly scoped crate or module
agent work log shows touches to files not listed in the task's scope fence
the real acceptance criterion (e.g., workspace CI gate) is broader than the task's stated file scope
invariants: Every out-of-fence file must be independently built and tested before acceptance.
The violation must be documented in the work log regardless of whether the change is accepted or reverted.
Acceptance requires both correctness AND a valid justification tied to real acceptance criteria.
produces: A validated, documented decision (accept or revert) for each out-of-fence change, recorded in the task work log

name: live-model-dimension-discovery-via-probe-embed
description: Probe the live embedding endpoint with a minimal test call and read the actual vector length instead of hardcoding dimensions, so the system automatically handles model changes without stale constants.
use_when: Embedding model is configurable via environment variable
Adding a second embedding model with a different output dimension
Service boots with OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL set to an unknown or new model
invariants: The dimension passed to Qdrant's ensure_collection must come from discover_dimension, not a hardcoded constant.
discover_dimension must be called before any collection creation or vector upsert.
produces: EmbeddingModelInfo { model_name, dimension } validated against the live model at startup

name: rust-eliminate-expect-with-sum-types
description: Replace runtime `.expect()` assertions on orchestration invariants with a sum type (enum) that makes the invalid state unrepresentable at compile time, reducing runtime panics to zero.
use_when: Rust code has .expect() calls in production hot paths asserting a structural invariant
an orchestration or state machine has a combination of fields that must always co-occur
code review finds 'Orchestrated without seams' or equivalent impossible-but-asserted states
invariants: The invalid state combination must be completely unrepresentable after the refactor — if the compiler can still construct it, the goal was not met
No new .expect() sites may be introduced as part of this refactor
produces: 0 live .expect() sites for the targeted invariant class (verified by grep)

description: DDL migration scripts that contain an explicit COMMIT statement silently escape any wrapping sqlx Transaction, leaving subsequent operations (e.g. tracking table INSERT) outside the transaction and voiding atomicity.
use_when: migration apply wraps DDL in pool.begin() but atomicity of tracking INSERT vs DDL is uncertain
a migration test passes yet a rollback-proof assertion is absent
DDL migration script was authored with an explicit COMMIT; inside it
invariants: An explicit COMMIT inside a migration script body terminates the enclosing transaction immediately, regardless of any outer sqlx Transaction wrapper.
A rollback-proof integration test (deliberate failure → assert side-effect absent) is the only reliable proof that atomicity holds.
produces: Confirmed atomic migration: DDL and tracking INSERT either both commit or both roll back, verified by a failing rollback-proof test becoming green

name: Before working on any task, thoroughly read all (preference)
description: Standing user preference: Before working on any task, thoroughly read all implemented plans up to v-1-5, trace every logic path, inspect every part of the repo, and understand all interfaces and how the pieces connect.

name: hybrid-search-zero-uplift-diagnosis
description: When BM25+dense hybrid search returns results identical to pure dense, the root cause is almost always that the extra multi-view fields BM25 indexes (tools, artifacts, invariants) are unpopulated in the corpus — not that the hybrid pipeline is broken.
use_when: hybrid search (BM25+dense) shows identical MRR/nDCG to pure dense
snapshot_hybrid and snapshot_dense return same ranked list
BM25 arm adds zero uplift to retrieval metrics
investigating why hybrid search provides no benefit
artifacts: corpus skill records with multi-view fields (tools, artifacts, invariants)
invariants: BM25 can only surface candidates the dense arm misses if those candidates contain terms in fields that embeddings blur; if the corpus has no such content, parity is mathematically expected.
Per-query score-level comparison is required to rule out 'BM25 engages but ties' vs 'BM25 never engages'.
produces: a confirmed root-cause (empty multi-view fields vs. pipeline bug) and a specific corpus-enrichment gate before re-evaluating

name: Always ensure all drifts and issues are captured (preference)
description: Standing user preference: Always ensure all drifts and issues are captured comprehensively.

name: fight-ai-workflow-bloat-with-single-source-references
description: Multi-phase AI prompting pipelines that re-emit the same WHY/context block into every artifact and every agent prompt fight drift through duplication, which itself causes plan bloat; the fix is author-once + reference, with each downstream artifact carrying only a pointer and one sentence of local intent.
use_when: plans or artifacts produced by a multi-phase AI pipeline are consistently too long
the same WHY / context block appears verbatim in 3+ artifacts
a 'deepening' or 'research' phase appends raw agent output and a separate compression skill exists to undo it
designing or refactoring a multi-phase prompting workflow (brainstorm → plan → architecture → tickets → work → review)
invariants: Each concept (WHY, TDD gate, severity levels, context tiers) must be defined in exactly one place; all other sites reference it.
A research/deepen phase must integrate findings, not append them — the artifact size budget is an invariant, not a suggestion.
produces: Plans that fit on roughly one screen with execution slices as the spine
Zero paragraph appearing more than once across all artifacts in the pipeline

name: sequence-clustered-fixes-smallest-to-absorbing-refactor
description: When executing multiple fixes that overlap the same file cluster, sequence from narrowest-scope first to broadest/most-restructuring last, and explicitly assign smaller residual cleanups as absorbed by the final refactor.
use_when: multiple pending fixes touch overlapping files and need execution ordering
a broad structural refactor (e.g., O(kN) join elimination, dedup extraction) could subsume smaller cleanups in the same file
planning a batch sprint across a known file cluster (e.g., bm25.rs / sparse.rs / dual_scope.rs)
invariants: The absorbing (last) fix must be executed after all narrower fixes in the same cluster, or it will overwrite unmerged work
Absorption must be explicitly declared before execution starts — implicit assumptions lead to double-implementation or merge loss
produces: a sequenced execution plan with explicit absorption assignments per cluster
zero double-touches within a cluster during batch execution

name: pre-existing-clippy-regression-triage
description: When cargo clippy fails on files not touched by the current branch, confirm pre-existing ownership via git log before marking the failure as a regression — avoids blocking a clean batch on inherited debt.
use_when: cargo clippy fails on a crate you didn't change
CI goes red with await_holding_lock or similar lint in test code
Determining whether clippy errors are regressions from current work vs inherited debt
invariants: Never count a pre-existing lint failure as a current-batch regression.
Every identified pre-existing failure must be filed as a cleanup todo with file:line, not silently skipped.
produces: Clear classification of each clippy error as: current-batch regression (must fix) vs pre-existing debt (must document)

name: cargo-clippy-workspace-all-targets-includes-examples-and-e2e
description: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings includes examples/ and tests/ (e2e and integration), not just lib; a per-crate clean pass does not guarantee the workspace merge gate passes.
use_when: cargo clippy -p {crate} exits 0 but the CI workspace clippy gate still fails
a ticket scopes clippy work to one crate but workspace exit 0 is the acceptance criterion
lint errors appear in examples/ or tests/e2e/ that were not visible in the per-crate run
invariants: `--all-targets` must be present to include examples/ and integration tests
Workspace gate AC means `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0, not any crate-scoped subset
produces: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0

name: ollama-thinking-model-think-false-structured-json
description: When calling an Ollama ''thinking'' model (gemma4, deepseek-r1, qwq, etc.) for structured JSON output, set `think: false` in the request or the model bleeds chain-of-thought reasoning into JSON keys, producing wrong-shaped output that silently deserializes to empty candidates.
use_when: Ollama structured call returns 0 candidates despite valid JSON and no error
gemma4 / deepseek-r1 / qwq / thinking model returns JSON with keys like 'thought1', 'thought2' instead of the contracted schema
structured extraction is reliable at temp>0 but deterministically fails at temp=0
serde deserializes Ollama response to empty vec with no parse error
invariants: Every structured Ollama call targeting a thinking model must include `think: false` in the request payload.
`think: false` must be set at ALL call sites for the model — partial application leaves latent flakiness.
produces: Deterministically correct JSON shape (`{"candidates":[...]}`) at temp=0 from the thinking model
5/5 (or N/N) reliable structured extraction runs

name: read-before-edit-file
description: Resolves a write-blocked error by reading the target file first before attempting any edits to it.

name: merge-coupled-todos-into-one-agent-unit
description: When two or more todos both modify the same specific code block or dispatch table, merge them into a single agent dispatch to avoid conflicting partial rewrites.
use_when: two todos both rewrite the same from_str/as_str dispatch block
two tasks modify overlapping lines in the same function
a pair of tasks would produce a merge conflict if dispatched independently
invariants: A merged unit must have a single agent apply all changes atomically; do not split the application across two sequential agents.
produces: A single diff that resolves both todos in one consistent rewrite of the shared code block

name: recursive-watcher-exclude-build-dirs
description: Exclude build-artifact and VCS directories from both WalkDir scans and recursive notify/inotify watch registrations to prevent near-100% CPU spin.
use_when: a service using WalkDir or the `notify` crate is pegged at ~100% CPU
recursive file watcher scans the whole repo including `target/` or `.git/`
graph-builder or file-indexing service spins after startup
invariants: The exclusion denylist must be applied to both the directory walk AND the recursive watch registration — one without the other still causes the spin.
produces: CPU usage drops to low single-digit percent; only source files are watched

name: search-arm-comparison-extend-to-top10-with-scores
description: Conclusively compare two search arms by diffing top-10 results on set membership, rank order, AND numeric scores per query — aggregate MRR/nDCG alone can mask complete arm equivalence.
use_when: comparing two retrieval arms (e.g. dense vs hybrid) and aggregate MRR/nDCG are identical
investigating whether BM25 component has any effect on final results
need conclusive evidence that two search configurations are equivalent
invariants: Set membership, rank order, and score-level comparison are three independent checks — all three must match for arms to be declared equivalent.
A verdict cache must be used consistently across both arms to avoid judge variability confounding score differences.
produces: a per-query, three-dimension diff table confirming or refuting arm equivalence with no ambiguity

name: On resuming after a break, pick up the (preference)
description: Standing user preference: On resuming after a break, pick up the last task directly — do not acknowledge the summary, recap what was happening, or preface with phrases like ''I''ll continue''.

name: claude-cli-headless-json-fence-stripping
description: When using `claude --print --output-format json`, the assistant text in `.result` is wrapped in triple-backtick json fences that must be stripped before JSON.parse(); failure to strip silently produces a parse error or corrupt object.
use_when: using `claude --print --output-format json` to drive extraction or structured-output pipelines
JSON.parse on claude CLI output throws SyntaxError or returns unexpected string
building a provider that calls the claude CLI instead of the Anthropic Messages API
invariants: `.result` must have code fences stripped before it is treated as raw JSON
Auth is the local subscription credential — the binary must exist on the host; it cannot run inside a container
produces: A parsed JSON object from the assistant's structured reply, ready for schema validation

name: verify-clippy-ci-gate-with-d-warnings
description: When a claim says 'clippy blocks CI', verify by checking if the CI pipeline uses `-- -D warnings`; bare cargo clippy always exits 0 on warnings without that flag.
use_when: a todo or bug report claims 'CI gate is red' or 'merge is blocked' due to cargo clippy warnings
need to verify whether `await_holding_lock` or other clippy lints actually block a PR merge
cargo clippy exits 0 locally but CI reportedly fails
invariants: `cargo clippy` exit code 0 does NOT imply warnings are absent; it only implies no hard errors without `-D warnings`.
Only when CI invokes `-- -D warnings` are warnings promoted to merge-blocking errors.
produces: Confirmed gate status: whether clippy warnings are merge-blocking in CI or merely advisory

name: model-keyed-qdrant-collections-multi-arm
description: Use model-slug-derived collection names (e.g. skills__<slug>) to let multiple embedding model arms coexist in Qdrant without dimension collision or requiring teardown between arms.
use_when: Adding a second embedding model to an existing Qdrant-backed search system
Running A/B measurement arms with different embedding dimensions (e.g. 768 vs 2560)
Need two embedding backends to coexist without full re-index on each switch
invariants: Each distinct (base_collection, model) pair maps to exactly one Qdrant collection.
The dimension used to create the collection must equal the discovered dimension of the active model.
produces: Two (or more) coexisting Qdrant collections, each valid for its own model and dimension, switchable via env var

name: extraction-pipeline-session-lifecycle-hook-coverage
description: An LLM-session extraction pipeline triggered only on UserPromptSubmit will miss session-end extraction, pre-compaction re-injection, and session-start context loading; all relevant lifecycle events must be explicitly wired.
use_when: an extraction or indexing pipeline is triggered by Claude Code / agent harness session hooks
skills extracted from a session are never persisted because the session ends without triggering extraction
context injected at session start is lost after compaction
`UserPromptSubmit` is the only wired hook but the system needs session-end or compaction awareness
the self-growing loop has no automatic trigger
invariants: Every data-flow requirement (inject, extract, re-inject on compaction) must map to exactly one lifecycle hook; a gap in hook coverage is a silent data loss, not a graceful degradation
produces: All session lifecycle events that affect context or extraction are handled
Extraction fires on session end; context survives compaction; injection fires on session start

name: orchestrator-must-verify-agent-results-independently
description: Never accept an agent's self-reported 'all tests pass' or 'build green' as final; the orchestrator must re-run build and tests independently, because agents may use validation commands with systematic blind spots.
use_when: sub-agent reports 'all tests pass' or 'build green' in a multi-agent orchestration workflow
the agent's stated validation method (e.g., `cargo check` or per-crate `cargo test`) may not cover all compilation units
one agent's output is a prerequisite for a subsequent agent's work
invariants: An agent's self-reported 'green' is insufficient evidence; the orchestrator must validate with commands the agent may not have run
Advancing to a dependent wave before independent validation multiplies the blast radius of any hidden failure
produces: Confirmed-green state — build and tests verified by the orchestrator independently — before the next dependency wave is unblocked

name: When an issue is already being actively addressed (preference)
description: Standing user preference: When an issue is already being actively addressed, do not fixate on it — acknowledge it briefly and move on.

name: Operate as a coding harness agent using the (preference)
description: Standing user preference: Operate as a coding harness agent using the provided system as your dynamic context layer.

name: fix-askuserquestion-options-overflow
description: Resolve an AskUserQuestion InputValidationError caused by exceeding the 4-option limit per question by auditing and trimming option arrays before re-invoking.

name: relevance-floor-fragility-on-small-corpus
description: A no-match relevance threshold calibrated on fewer than ~50 examples with a positive/negative class gap below 0.05 will break in production on larger, heterogeneous corpora. The gap will close, causing false positives or false negatives at scale.
use_when: setting a no-match or relevance cutoff threshold for a retrieval system
threshold was calibrated on fewer than 50 examples or with a positive/negative gap under 0.05
retrieval system starts returning irrelevant results or spurious no-match on production queries
invariants: Relevance threshold calibration corpus must cover the real distribution of production query and item types
The gap between the max negative-class score and min positive-class score must be >= 0.05 to be considered stable
produces: a stable no-match floor with documented false-positive/false-negative rates on a held-out set

name: silent-path-success-as-diagnostic-red-herring
description: When a system component returns 'success' silently — no error, zero score, empty result set, or an `unwrap_or_default()` default — under conditions where real output was expected, the root cause is almost always a silent None/empty fallback hiding a missing or misconfigured implementation, not a logic error in the surrounding code. Diagnosing the surrounding code first wastes multiple investigation cycles.
use_when: A retrieval or scoring arm returns zero scores or an empty result set without raising an error.
Ablating a component produces identical output to the unablated system — suggesting the component was never reached.
A BM25 or embedding index returns no results on queries known to match.
A pipeline step appears to complete successfully but downstream metrics are unchanged.
invariants: A silent success with zero-score output is never a 'correct' result for a component whose job is to produce non-zero signal.
Replacing a silent fallback with a loud failure must happen before further diagnosis — otherwise later steps investigate the wrong layer.
produces: Confirmation that the implementation gap is the root cause, not a logic bug
A loud failure that surfaces the gap to the next caller

name: migration-file-unwired-from-registry
description: In explicit-array migration systems, a SQL file can exist on disk but never be added to the MIGRATIONS registry — it silently never applies on boot; always verify array contiguity when wiring a new migration.
use_when: adding a new entry to a MIGRATIONS array and discovering contiguous predecessors are missing
boot migration run applies fewer migrations than there are SQL files on disk
a CHECK constraint migration activates on boot for the first time in production
invariants: The MIGRATIONS array must be contiguous — every file on disk must have a wired entry, in order.
A retroactively-wired migration must be idempotent before it can be safely applied to existing databases.
Activating a CHECK constraint requires all existing rows and future writers to comply.
produces: Contiguous, fully-wired MIGRATIONS array with idempotent entries and a passing migration-ordering test

name: configuration-default-silent-misrouting
description: Configuration defaults — env-var fallbacks such as `${VAR:-./local}`, auto-derived paths, and implicit scope assignments — silently route operations to unintended locations when the explicit value is absent or misset. This is especially dangerous when a mount, store, or routing key is intended to be machine-global but defaults to a project-local path, causing data to land in the wrong scope with no error and no observable failure at the call site.
use_when: Writing Docker Compose volume mounts or service config with env-var substitution
Designing any config system where values route to different scopes (project-local vs global vs shared)
Reviewing .env.example or compose files for correctness of defaults
invariants: A config default must never silently change the operational scope (local vs global, project vs shared) of a store, mount, or routing key
produces: Fail-fast or correctly-routed config with no silent misrouting

description: Standing user preference: Execution agents should always use the Sonnet model.

name: docker-healthcheck-tool-absent-in-minimal-image
description: Docker healthchecks using wget/curl/nc silently fail forever on minimal images that don't ship those binaries; always verify probe binaries exist inside the target image before writing a HEALTHCHECK.
use_when: container reports 'Unhealthy' but the service responds correctly to HTTP requests from the host
healthcheck CMD uses wget or curl in a non-debian/ubuntu-based or distroless image
qdrant, alpine-based, or other scratch/minimal images show perpetual Unhealthy status
invariants: A Docker HEALTHCHECK CMD must only invoke binaries that are present inside the container filesystem at runtime — a missing binary causes an immediate non-zero exit, identical to an unhealthy service.
produces: Healthcheck transitions from perpetual Unhealthy to Healthy when the service is actually up
